The authors define security through a simulation paradigm and give the first generic simulation-secure public-key MHFE construction for all polynomial-size circuits, built from any IND-secure standard functional encryption for circuits.

entry.title: Adaptive Leaky LWE and Its Security
entry.summary: Adaptive Leaky LWE and Its Security IACR ePrint · Nov 9, 2026This paper studies an adaptive variant of the Leaky LWE problem, which asks whether LWE samples remain pseudorandom given noisy linear information about the secret and error. Here each leakage matrix may depend on the challenge and all earlier leakage answers. Under explicit norm, smoothing, and sampling conditions, the authors reduce Gaussian-secret LWE to this problem for polynomially many rounds. The reduction preserves the public-matrix distribution and access to its correlated oracle, and supports rectangular leakage matrices and non-spherical discrete Gaussians over arbitrary number-field orders.

entry.title: DKG: A framework that uses a two-layer knowledge graph and an LLM to automate side-channel key recovery on cryptosystems
entry.summary: DKG: A Dual-Layer Knowledge Graph and LLM Co-Driven Framework for Fully Automated Side-Channel Analysis of Cryptosystems IACR ePrint · Nov 9, 2026This paper presents DKG, a framework in which a two-layer knowledge graph and a large language model work together to automatically carry out side-channel attacks that recover cryptographic keys. The upper layer holds configuration components and the lower layer holds diagnostic strategies, linked by cross-layer relationships, and the graph is built from 166 technical documents without manual annotation. On eight datasets covering AES, DES, and SM4 across smartcards, FPGAs, and MCUs, DKG with DeepSeek-V3.2 reaches a 97.5% end-to-end key-recovery success rate, compared with 68.8% for the text-retrieval agent ReAct-RAG.

entry.title: Practical Confidential Clustering for Federated Learning Using Efficient Secret Sharing
entry.summary: Practical Confidential Clustering for Federated Learning using Efficient Secret-Sharing IACR ePrint · Nov 9, 2026This paper presents CCFL, a framework that groups similar clients in federated learning so each group can train a personalized sub-model, while keeping the clustering confidential. Distance computations and centroid updates run entirely on encrypted data using Replicated Secret Sharing, supported by an anonymizing server that shuffles data and multi-party computation. The authors report up to 46.7 times computational speedup under LAN and WAN conditions and claim a better privacy-utility trade-off than existing personalized federated learning methods.

entry.title: MPCTM: Privacy-preserving collision checking for drone and autonomous vehicle paths using multi-party computation
entry.summary: MPCTM: MPC-Based Trajectory Matching on Unmanned Autonomous Systems IACR ePrint · Nov 9, 2026This paper presents MPCTM, a privacy-preserving trajectory matching protocol built on multi-party computation (MPC) that detects possible collisions between pre-planned paths of unmanned autonomous systems without revealing extra information. The model captures collisions occurring between discretely sampled points, and a lightweight MPC-friendly variant is also proposed, with its accuracy-efficiency trade-off discussed. Compared with the closest prior solution, the authors report over 2x lower online latency in dealer mode for the full model and 8x for the lightweight model, while autonomous mode is 2.5-3x slower but with no false negatives.

entry.title: Using Ascon-based designs to encrypt computer memory
entry.summary: Enabling Memory Encryption Using Ascon Derivatives IACR ePrint · Nov 10, 2026This paper examines how to protect data stored in memory against an attacker with physical access, using Ascon as the core building block. Memory encryption must handle fine-grained accesses of 256 to 512 bits while meeting strict latency, area, and energy limits. The authors report that Ascon-based constructions outperform AES-based HCTR2, can compete with XTS-AES, and support larger block sizes.

entry.title: Necessary antipodal quadratic term for degree-three rotation symmetric bent functions
entry.summary: Antipodal necessity for rotation symmetric bent functions of degree at most three IACR ePrint · Nov 10, 2026The paper studies rotation symmetric Boolean functions of degree at most three. It proves that if such a function in an even number of variables is bent, its algebraic normal form must contain the antipodal quadratic orbit. As a consequence, no homogeneous rotation symmetric cubic Boolean function is bent. The proof relies only on finite Fourier analysis and linear algebra over the binary field.

entry.title: Cost trade-offs in mixed-mode oblivious RAM
entry.summary: Access Cost Tradeoffs in Mixed-Mode Oblivious RAM IACR ePrint · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies mixed-mode oblivious RAM (ORAM), where each memory request is marked either public, which reveals its address, or private, which hides it. It analyzes how much work such schemes must perform, and which requests must perform it, in the cell-probe model with a passive server. The analysis covers the expected amortized per-request cost on randomized workloads with independent modes and uniformly random addresses. The main result is a tight tradeoff between the cost of public reads and private writes.

entry.title: TUTTI: Parallel CKKS Bootstrapping in Under 3 ms on CPU
entry.summary: TUTTI: Parallel CKKS Bootstrapping in under 3 ms on CPU IACR ePrint · Nov 10, 2026The paper presents TUTTI, a new CKKS bootstrapping procedure that improves on the SPRU approach with better parallelism and more messages per operation, plus a refined security analysis of LMSS block-binary secret keys. On 192 threads it bootstraps 4096 real-number messages in 46 to 83.4 ms, up to three times faster than SHIP on the same machine. For a single message on 32 threads it takes 4.6 ms, compared with 7.3 ms for TFHE-rs, and the advantage also holds on an Apple M5 Pro laptop.

entry.title: γ₁₁: A Finite Spectral Relaxation for the Macadamia 0008 Form
entry.summary: γ₁₁: A Finite Spectral Relaxation — the macadamia 0008 IACR ePrint · Nov 9, 2026The paper studies the lattice constant γ₁₁=4/¹¹√972 by reducing it to conditions on chains of lattices of ranks 11, 10 and 9. It settles the case of the perfect form 0008, showing that every admissible chain marked by this form has determinant at least 972. The proof is computer-assisted, with remaining cases excluded by finite exact-arithmetic checks. ★★★★ Notable: The authors reduce the gamma_11 bound to a finite spectral relaxation and report a computer-assisted exclusion of one perfect form's chains via rational certificates.

entry.title: Contact geometry for γ₁₁: four macadamia forms
entry.summary: γ₁₁: Contact Geometry — the macadamias 0001, 0014, 0059 and 0015 IACR ePrint · Nov 9, 2026This paper continues a series on the Hermite constant γ₁₁ and settles four remaining cases, the macadamia perfect forms 0001, 0014, 0059 and 0015. It uses the contact geometry of each form to bound the covering radius of a reference lattice, and a primitive-extension inequality then gives det L ≥ 972. The proof is computer-assisted, with each finite check linked to records in a certificate archive. ★★★★ Notable: The authors settle four remaining candidate lattices for the Hermite constant γ₁₁ with one contact-geometry method, using computer-assisted verification.

entry.title: Secure Information Flow in Quantum Programs: Definitions, Verification, and Examples
entry.summary: Secure Information Flow in Quantum Programs arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies how to prevent confidential information from leaking through the execution of quantum programs. It proposes two security definitions, a noninterference-based one generalizing the classical notion and a simulation-based one that explicitly models an attacker, and proves they are equivalent. To verify security, the authors build a proof framework on quantum Hoare logic and introduce self-conjugation, a new technique that replaces standard self-composition, which fails in the quantum setting. The framework is demonstrated on examples from the quantum one-time pad, quantum error correction, and anonymous entanglement generation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give two equivalent security definitions and a self-conjugation technique bypassing no-cloning, demonstrated on quantum one-time pad examples.

entry.title: Sable: A small-field sumcheck proof system for bit-exact inference of large language models
entry.summary: Sable: A Small-Field Sumcheck Argument for Bit-Exact Inference of Large Language Models arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper presents Sable, an argument system and single-GPU prover that proves a committed integer-quantized transformer produced a given token sequence from a prompt, bit for bit. The inference is defined by an integer function with no floating-point steps, and the constraints are designed so they never wrap modulo the 31-bit KoalaBear prime. On one NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU, the authors report proving all 64 layers of Qwen2.5-32B for 4,096 tokens in 92.5 seconds. ★★★★ Notable: The authors present a small-field sumcheck argument proving bit-exact integer LLM inference, reporting prover times on Qwen models and releasing code.

entry.title: What a CAGE 4 Score Measures: An Audit of a Learned Cyber-Defense Benchmark
entry.summary: What a CAGE 4 Score Measures: An Audit of a Learned Cyber-Defense Benchmark, Its Reference Defenders, and the Tables Built on Them arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper reproduces two reference defenders, KEEP and H-MARL Expert, for the CAGE Challenge 4 cyber-defense benchmark. It finds that the simulator silently discards actions sent to agents still busy with a previous action, and that the documented observation does not expose this busy state, affecting reported scores and training outcomes. The authors also note that evaluation fixes the environment seed but not the policy seed, and that five published comparison tables omit the details needed to compare their numbers. The authors release their tools, patches, traces, checkpoints and a disclosure checklist. ★★★★ Notable: The authors reproduce reference defenders and report that busy-agent actions are silently discarded and mis-scored, quantifying score shifts and auditing five published tables.

entry.title: Pulse or Provenance? Checking What rPPG Deepfake Detectors Actually Learn
entry.summary: Pulse or Provenance? What rPPG-Based Deepfake Detectors Learn arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper examines whether rPPG-based deepfake detectors rely on genuine heart-rate signals. Controlled experiments on Celeb-DF++ and FaceForensics++ indicate the detectors mainly pick up on video source characteristics rather than physiological pulse. The authors also report that official Celeb-DF splits share identities and source videos between training and test sets. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show rPPG detectors learn video provenance and high-frequency artifacts rather than physiology, using controlled experiments on Celeb-DF++ and FF++, a caution for evaluation.

entry.title: A proof that no finite rulebook can certify every safe AI-generated program
entry.summary: No finite rulebook can certify every safe program: an impossibility theorem for gatekeeping AI agents arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper asks whether a gatekeeper can decide from code alone which AI-written programs may run, given rules that must be backed by finite, machine-checkable evidence. It proves that complete allow and deny rulebooks are impossible: prohibitions can only be caught when violated, never cleared for good, while confidentiality and responsiveness cannot be settled either way. The authors also show that a sound rulebook of n bits omits a compliant program of about n bits, and they offer a weaker guarantee: a checkable list that includes all required allowances and excludes all refusals. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove finite checkable evidence cannot certify all safe programs, characterize confidentiality and responsiveness rules, and bound rulebook size.

entry.title: How Well Do SAST Tools Work Across Languages? An OCPP Case Study
entry.summary: How Well Do SAST Tools Work Across Languages? An Empirical Study Using OCPP Implementations arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper evaluates how well static application security testing (SAST) tools detect issues across programming languages, using twelve OCPP 1.6 implementations for electric vehicle charging stations, each written in a different language. The authors applied SonarQube, Semgrep, and language-specific analyzers. Reported issues ranged from two in Rust to 1,689 in Java, which the authors attribute likely to differences in the maturity of SAST tool ecosystems rather than inherent code quality.

entry.title: MammothDP: Privacy-Protected Boosted Decision Trees for Trusted Hardware
entry.summary: MammothDP: Private Boosted Decision Trees Ready for Trusted Hardware and Leakage-free Hyperparameters arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper presents MammothDP, a machine learning system built on the gradient boosted decision tree learner S-BDT for protecting sensitive tabular data, such as in the European Health Data Space. It runs on a trusted execution environment (TEE) with timing side-channel hardening and is provably differentially private when used within a privacy filter. To improve the privacy-utility tradeoff, the authors introduce an early stopping criterion that selects the number of trees without privacy overhead, and an improved rollback protection that resists timing side-channel attacks.

entry.title: Location Matters: Sparse Latent-Variance Attacks for Face Privacy against Diffusion Personalization
entry.summary: Location Matters: Sparse Latent-Variance Attacks for Face Privacy against Diffusion Personalization arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper introduces SEAL, a method that protects face photos from being used by diffusion models to learn and reproduce a person's identity. SEAL modifies only 5% of spatial locations in a facial image, using a differentiable top-k masking scheme and a variance-based objective on the frozen VAE encoder's latent distribution. Experiments on CelebA-HQ and VGGFace2 report protected-image quality exceeding 41 dB PSNR, 0.97 SSIM, and at most 0.07 LPIPS, with identity similarity reduced to at most 0.15 after personalization.

entry.title: Model-based method for creating SOC simulation exercises for cybersecurity training
entry.summary: Model-Based Authoring of SOC Simulation Exercises for Cybersecurity Education arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper presents a model-based method for authoring virtual Security Operations Center (SOC) exercises for cybersecurity education. A technical and educational specification is used to build an incident exercise model, and a large language model generates selected scenario text based on it. The method was implemented in a Virtual SOC prototype and evaluated with a phishing-to-ransomware reference exercise, where a separate validator checked references, ordering, evidence links and assessment completeness. The resulting exercise package ran in the Virtual SOC learner environment, indicating the approach is feasible.

entry.title: Empirical Study of CVE Vulnerability Propagation Within and Between Software Projects
entry.summary: An Empirical Study on CVE-based Vulnerabilities Propagation from one System to another System (IntraProject vs InterProject) arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper analyzes how CVE-based vulnerabilities propagate within and between software projects, using NVD data and the SQVDT detection tool. The authors found similar vulnerable code patterns in Linux, Android, and thousands of GitHub open-source projects. Several high-severity (CVSS) vulnerabilities spread from one system to another through copy-pasted code, and the study verifies these patterns and their frequency while recommending attention to their impact on interconnected systems.

entry.title: GARD: A gradient-guided method that repairs backdoors in multimodal contrastive learning models
entry.summary: GARD: Gradient-Guided Adversarial Representation Defense against Backdoors in Multimodal Contrastive Learning Models arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper addresses backdoor attacks on multimodal contrastive learning models such as CLIP, which can use triggers of many structures. It proposes GARD, a post-hoc defense that needs no knowledge of the attack target or trigger, using global and local adversarial probes to perturb representations and then realign them with clean anchors while preserving image-text alignment. Across six visual backdoor attacks and two CLIP visual backbones, GARD reduces the attack success rate below 1% in all 12 combinations while keeping competitive clean accuracy.

entry.title: Isolation Is Not Confidentiality: Limits of Geometric Access Control in RAG
entry.summary: Isolation Is Not Confidentiality: Security Boundaries of Geometric Access Control in RAG arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper analyzes the security of geometric access-control methods for retrieval-augmented generation systems, which transform embeddings so that documents under different policies stay separated during search. The authors evaluate policy isolation, representation confidentiality, query forgery resistance, and policy-membership hiding against curious cloud providers and users. They find that these transformations preserve retrieval utility and provide strong policy isolation, but do not guarantee the other security properties.

entry.title: Reconstructing client data from gradients using linear and affine subspace constraints
entry.summary: Gradient Inversion through Linear and Affine Subspace Constraints arXiv · Nov 10, 2026In federated learning, gradients shared by clients can leak sensitive information about their local data. The paper shows that aggregate gradients from a fully connected layer, with correct scaling, form an affine combination of its inputs. It uses known linear or affine subspace information at each layer to improve gradient inversion attacks. The authors report substantial reconstruction gains in some settings and also examine batch size overestimation and differential privacy noise.

entry.title: Comparing WeChat and Telegram MiniApp security designs for cross-platform analysis
entry.summary: Comparing WeChat and Telegram MiniApp Security Architectures: Toward Cross-Platform Analysis arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper qualitatively compares the security architectures of WeChat Mini Programs and Telegram MiniApps, based on official documentation, prior research, and manual analysis of a specific Telegram Android source revision. It uses a shared taxonomy of security controls, assets, and threat sources to examine execution environments, communication paths, and trust boundaries. WeChat provides a dedicated MiniApp runtime, while Telegram combines web execution with host controls, and both leave backend authentication and resource authorization to developers. The authors do not rank the ecosystems by security or claim validated vulnerability detection.

entry.title: From Attack Surface to Defense Architecture: Compositional Security for Agentic Coding Harnesses
entry.summary: From Attack Surface to Defense Architecture: Compositional Security for Agentic Coding Harnesses arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper examines security risks in AI coding tools that connect language models to shells, filesystems, and network sockets, where injected instructions can turn common system programs into attack tools. The authors propose ActiveSecHarness, a neurosymbolic reference-monitor architecture combining capability tokens, a two-dimensional taint lattice, and audit mechanisms. Tested on 252 fixtures, its deterministic lowest-level guard blocked all attacks with no false positives, running far faster than an LLM-based judge.

entry.title: Data4Cyber: A labeled cyber-physical dataset for distribution-grid control systems under typical industrial attacks
entry.summary: Data4Cyber: Labeled Cyber-Physical Datasets for Distribution-Grid Management Systems Under Representative OT Attacks arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper presents Data4Cyber, a labeled cyber-physical dataset recorded in a laboratory distribution management system for self-consumption optimization with photovoltaic generation, battery storage, controllable loads, and substation metering. It combines synchronized process measurements, controller context, price incentives, and Modbus/TCP and MQTT packet captures across a benign baseline and six attack scenarios. The authors find that high recall alone is insufficient, since several detectors achieve sensitivity through alarm saturation, and that context-driven attacks require process-aware interpretation rather than single-channel thresholding.

entry.title: Research on acoustic side-channel attacks against keyboards that generalize across devices and use language models
entry.summary: Domain-Invariant and Language-Model-Assisted Acoustic Side-Channel Attacks on Keyboards arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies recovering typed text from keystroke sounds captured by an ordinary microphone, without access to the victim's device. Earlier work tested these attacks only in idealized lab conditions, so this paper examines whether they still work with unseen keyboards, different users, noisy environments, and compressed audio channels. It concludes that such inference remains possible when the acoustic model is made domain-invariant and its noisy predictions are corrected by a language model.

entry.title: Private knowledge retrieval and private inference for secure multi-agent AI systems
entry.summary: On Private Knowledge Retrieval and Private Inference for secure multi-agent systems arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper examines security risks in multi-agent systems built on large language models, focusing on memory poisoning attacks against semantic memory. The authors propose signing the knowledge base to prevent unwanted manipulation, building security into the design of semantic memory. Agents use a local Prolog-like inference system with Horn clauses that privately accesses this externally signed knowledge base. Python implementations are provided at different privacy levels, including k-anonymity and information-theoretic privacy (IT-PIR).

entry.title: BypassGym: A Benchmark for Testing AI Agents' Ability to Evade Endpoint Defenses
entry.summary: BypassGym: A Benchmark for Evaluating AI Agents' Endpoint Defense Evasion Capabilities arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper introduces BypassGym, a benchmark that systematically evaluates whether AI agents can evade endpoint detection and response (EDR) products. Agents must generate and compile a loader that runs command-and-control (C2) shellcode without being blocked or terminated. The evaluation runs on real Windows systems and EDR products inside virtual machines on Proxmox VE, testing 5 lightweight model backends against 6 EDR products and 3 payloads.

entry.title: MOAI: A Module-Optimizing Architecture for Non-Interactive Secure Transformer Inference
entry.summary: MOAI: Module-Optimizing Architecture for non-interactive secure transformer Inference arXiv · Nov 10, 2026MOAI is a homomorphic encryption (HE) based framework that performs transformer inference directly on encrypted inputs without interaction, so that cloud-hosted models can run without exposing user data. It improves efficiency through a unified column and diagonal packing scheme, rotation-free Softmax and LayerNorm algorithms, and interleaved batching that reduces costly HE rotations. Compared with THOR on BERT-base, it reduces evaluation time by 52.8%, and when applied to Powerformer it reduces time by 55.7%.

entry.title: POEM: An output-relative block-sparse attention method for faster long-context prefilling in language models
entry.summary: POEM: Output-Relative Block-Sparse Attention for Long-Context Prefilling arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper introduces POEM, a method for speeding up the prefilling stage of large language models when processing long inputs. It uses output-relative criteria to decide which attention blocks to keep, applying block-sparse attention to reduce computation. The paper reports that the approach improves efficiency while maintaining performance.

entry.title: TERM: Target-Free Jailbreak Defense via Entropy-Guided Residual Modulation
entry.summary: TERM: Target-Free Jailbreak Defense via Entropy-Guided Residual Modulation arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper proposes TERM, an inference-time defense that protects large language models against jailbreak attacks. It calibrates attention entropy deviations against each prompt's own prefill baseline and uses them to adaptively scale the model's own residual updates, without a predefined safety direction. The method is compared with seven defenses on seven jailbreak attacks and two over-refusal benchmarks across Llama, Qwen, and Gemma models. Results indicate improved jailbreak robustness, low over-refusal on benign safety-sensitive requests, and modest inference overhead.

entry.title: Data-efficient backdoor detection in federated learning via unlearning responses
entry.summary: Data-Efficient Unlearning-Based Backdoor Detection in Federated Learning arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper addresses detecting backdoor attacks in federated learning, where malicious clients manipulate the global model while keeping main-task performance intact. It proposes SURA, which reuses a small clean proxy dataset across multiple train-mode loss-ascent steps to strengthen client responses. SURA restores the shared pre-probe batch normalization state at readout to remove drift caused by repeated probing. The authors report that across six backdoor attacks, SURA using only 10 clean server images outperforms methods under the same data budget and approaches the robustness of larger proxy sets.

entry.title: 5G CATS: A 5G-Based Cryptographic System to Verify Chip Location and Deter Smuggling
entry.summary: 5G CATS: 5G-Based Cryptographic Authorization Against Trafficking of Semiconductor Devices arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper presents 5G CATS, a system for verifying where AI accelerator chips operate after deployment. It places a 5G radio, cryptographic engine, and hardware interlock inside the GPU package and pairs them with 5G URLLC base stations. Round-trip time measurements are used to bound the chip's distance from a trusted landmark. Simulations show the approach narrows round-trip time variation and detects fiber relay attacks from much greater distances than default 5G.

entry.title: "Stinging the Swarm": Extracting Attacker Intelligence from a Twin-Controller OT Honeypot
entry.summary: Stinging the Swarm: Extracting Attacker Intelligence from a Twin-Controller OT Honeypot arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper presents Talos, an inline gate that judges AI agent requests to industrial controllers within milliseconds and redirects flagged agents to a mirror-twin decoy of the real plant. Evaluated against 2,400 autonomous attacker agents across four tiers of increasing concealment, no writes reached the real plant. The authors also describe behavioral patterns along persistence and disclosure axes, and show how involuntary signals across the swarm can build a high-confidence attacker profile.

entry.title: Veritas: A Verifier Generation Harness for Agent Tasks
entry.summary: Veritas: A Verifier Generation Harness for Agent Tasks arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper proposes Veritas, a harness that automatically generates verifiers to judge the outcome of each improvement round in self-improving systems, reducing the cost of hand-written verifiers. Veritas adds three mechanisms: an evidence header, a library of domain rules, and authoring principles partly refined by a self-improvement loop. Evaluated on six benchmarks, its generated verifiers agree better with official verdicts than seven other harnesses on all four execution-scored benchmarks.

entry.title: How much a partial view of a toric-code qubit leaks, and the Nishimori point
entry.summary: How wide must an eavesdropper be? Leakage of a toric-code logical bit to a strip and the Nishimori point arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper studies how much information a partial observer can learn about a logical bit in a fault-tolerant quantum computer by accessing only some of its qubits. It proves that, for any region and any Pauli noise, the observer's best advantage equals 1 minus twice the failure probability of maximum-likelihood decoding confined to that region. It also links the operational threshold of a two-row strip to the Nishimori point of the random-bond Ising model. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove the eavesdropper advantage equals 1-2P_fail for any region and Pauli noise, linking strip thresholds to the Nishimori point and testing on IBM hardware.

entry.title: Latent Barrier Steering: safer generative robot planning in two stages
entry.summary: Latent Barrier Steering: Hierarchical Safety for Generative Planning arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper introduces Latent Barrier Steering (LBS), a hierarchical framework for safe flow-matching-based generative planning. It first steers the generator's behavior latent toward rollouts with larger safety margins, then applies a path-space control-barrier-function quadratic program only to residual violations. Experiments on navigation and robot end-effector planning tasks show that LBS preserves safety while improving goal reaching and reducing correction burden compared with path-level safety filters.

entry.title: Quadratic Randomized Encodings for All Functions with Statistical Privacy
entry.summary: From Degree Three to Degree Two: Statistical Randomized Encodings for All Functions IACR ePrint · Nov 7, 2026The paper constructs quadratic randomized encodings for every Boolean function, with exponentially small correctness and statistical privacy errors. The encoding, decoder and simulator have complexity polynomial in the size of mod-2 branching programs and the security parameter. The results extend to multiparty encodings and yield applications such as one-way functions of output locality three and non-interactive client-server protocols. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors report quadratic statistical randomized encodings for every Boolean function with exponentially small errors, answering the open degree-two and locality-three questions and extending to mu

entry.title: More Keys, Less Commitment: Key-Committing Attacks on BBB Accordions and a New Transform
entry.summary: More Keys, Less Commitment: Key-Committing Attacks on BBB Accordions via Encode-then-Encipher and a Key-Committing Transform IACR ePrint · Nov 7, 2026This paper examines whether beyond-birthday-bound (BBB) security of cryptographic accordions strengthens key commitment in authenticated encryption built from them. It shows that extra keys introduced for BBB security give adversaries additional freedom, enabling O(1) key-committing attacks on many schemes, mostly built via Encode-then-Encipher. The authors propose CACH, a black-box transform from BBB-secure accordions to robust authenticated encryption with key-committing security, instantiated with CHCTR2. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show extra keys in BBB accordions enable O(1) key-committing attacks on several AE schemes and propose the CACH transform, with reported security bounds and performance comparisons.

entry.title: Removing padding in cryptography by proving the hardness of certifying random strings
entry.summary: Overcoming Padding in Cryptography via Hardness of Certifying Random Strings IACR ePrint · Nov 7, 2026Many cryptographic security proofs use hybrid arguments whose intermediate descriptions are larger than the real scheme, forcing the real scheme to be artificially padded. This superfluous padding blocks succinct primitives whose parameter sizes do not grow with input length. The paper introduces a framework that removes padding by linking cryptography to proof complexity through proof-complexity generators (PCGs). Its master theorem lifts security on compressible instances to all instances when PCGs exist. Applications include rate-1 iO, succinct witness encryption, succinct non-interactive arguments with short CRS for NP subclasses, and multi-input functional encryption for unbounded arity. ★★★★ Notable: The authors link cryptography and proof complexity via PCGs to eliminate padding, reporting applications to rate-1 iO and succinct witness encryption.

entry.title: Round-optimal statistical verifiable secret sharing with polynomial cost
entry.summary: Round-Optimal Statistical Verifiable Secret Sharing with Polynomial Complexity IACR ePrint · Nov 7, 2026This paper studies verifiable secret sharing (VSS), a cryptographic primitive that keeps secret distribution and reconstruction correct even when some participants are corrupt. Earlier work by Applebaum, Kachlon and Patra achieved round optimality but with communication exponential in the number of parties. This paper presents the first round-optimal statistical VSS for t<n/2 with polynomial communication and computation. The protocol is built from a new notion of weak secret sharing. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give the first round-optimal statistical VSS with polynomial communication and computation for t<n/2, via a new weak secret sharing notion.

entry.title: Minimum bucket size for reliable Path ORAM, a memory-access-hiding method
entry.summary: The Minimum Bucket Capacity for Reliable Path ORAM IACR ePrint · Nov 8, 2026Path ORAM hides memory access patterns by storing data blocks in a binary tree with buckets of capacity Z, and keeping blocks that do not fit in a client-side stash. The paper shows that Z=4 is the smallest bucket capacity giving a uniform exponential bound on stash overflow probability for binary Path ORAM. For Z=3, it constructs instances where a single sequential scan of all blocks produces a stash of size Ω(N) with probability bounded away from zero.'] ★★★★★ Notable: The authors report a uniform exponential stash bound at Z=4 and a linear lower bound at Z=3, giving a sharp threshold via an auxiliary independent-geometric model.

entry.title: Re-examining the Security of OleF, t-OleF, and OlÆF
entry.summary: Revisiting the Security of OleF, t-OleF, and OlÆF IACR ePrint · Nov 8, 2026This paper revisits the security of the online authenticated encryption schemes OleF, t-OleF, and OlÆF and identifies two independent flaws. It shows a mask-compensation relation between continuation and termination processing in OleF and t-OleF, which enables a two-query distinguisher against OleF and a similar attack on t-OleF using concrete AXU hash families. The attacks are extended to OlÆF, breaking its privacy and integrity. The paper also refutes a claimed ideal integrity bound for variable-expansion online authenticated encryption. ★★★★ Notable: The authors identify a mask-compensation relation in OleF and construct a two-query distinguisher, and report counterexamples refuting an ideal RUP bound.

entry.title: Incrementally Verifiable Oracle-Aided Computation: Short Proofs for AI Tasks That Use External Information
entry.summary: Incrementally Verifiable Oracle Aided Computation IACR ePrint · Nov 9, 2026This paper studies incrementally verifiable computation (IVC), which lets a prover keep a short proof that can be efficiently updated after each computation step without re-running earlier steps. Under the Learning with Errors (LWE) assumption, the authors construct IVC schemes for oracle-aided computations, which depend on external information and human judgment. They give privately verifiable constructions for robust computations and publicly verifiable constructions for oracles that sign their answers, and also prove a lower bound for certain publicly verifiable schemes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend IVC to oracle-aided computation, giving LWE-based constructions in robust and signed-oracle settings plus a lower bound.

entry.title: QUASI: Post-Quantum Quorum Attestation of Pre-Validated Statements
entry.summary: QUASI: Post-Quantum Quorum Attestation of Pre-Validated Statements IACR ePrint · Nov 7, 2026This paper introduces QUASI, a class of protocols that lets a group of parties produce a publicly verifiable attestation that a pre-validated statement is valid, for use in quorum-based systems. Each party only needs to authenticate a small subset of the statement's symbols for the quorum to attest to the whole. The scheme is built from hashing and error correction alone. Its main randomized construction reduces per-party contribution size and hash computations by more than 10 times compared with full hash-based signatures.

entry.title: Building Boolean and vector correctors that remove bias from random bits, including some beating the best linear designs
entry.summary: Constructions of Boolean Correctors with Optimal Nonlinearity and Vectorial Correctors Beyond Optimal Linear Correction Order IACR ePrint · Nov 7, 2026This paper studies correctors, postprocessing functions that remove statistical bias from raw bitstreams of physical random number generators. It develops a framework based on binary Krawtchouk polynomials and proves universal upper bounds on corrector nonlinearity. It gives constructions of Boolean correctors with optimal nonlinearity for correction order n-2 and asymptotically optimal ones for n-d-1. It also presents the first infinite family of nonlinear vectorial correctors whose correction order exceeds that of optimal linear correctors.

entry.title: Registration-based encryption with faster user registration
entry.summary: Registration-based Encryption with Logarithmic Registration IACR ePrint · Nov 7, 2026This paper presents a black-box, pairing-based registration-based encryption (RBE) construction in which users generate their own keys and a Key Curator manages only registered public keys. Built on a multilinear tree, registering a user updates only the corresponding root-to-leaf path. Experiments show registration and key generation complete in milliseconds when the maximum capacity is 10^7 users.

entry.title: Jazzline: Composable CryptoLine Proofs of Correctness for Jasmin Programs
entry.summary: Jazzline: Composable CryptoLine Functional Correctness Proofs for Jasmin Programs IACR ePrint · Nov 7, 2026Jasmin is a language for fast, high-assurance cryptography, and its correctness proofs are usually done deductively in EasyCrypt, which scales poorly for low-level architecture-specific code. This paper shows how to soundly use CryptoLine, a semi-automatic verification tool, to discharge subgoals in functional correctness proofs of complex Jasmin programs. The authors extend Jasmin with annotations and provide an automatic translation into a CryptoLine model, with most complex transformations certified. They also formalize and implement automatic extraction of the semantics of a CryptoLine proof.

entry.title: A systematic survey of virtual machines over fully homomorphic encryption
entry.summary: SoK: Understanding Virtual Machines over Fully Homomorphic Encryption IACR ePrint · Nov 7, 2026This paper surveys research on fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) from a virtual machine perspective, compiling more than 125 works. It identifies three forms of FHE virtual machines: SISD, SIMD, and hybrid. The authors also discuss how FHE compilers and hardware accelerators can improve their usability and performance. Experiments test eight VM instructions and two end-to-end applications to compare design trade-offs, concluding that each VM type has distinct characteristics and that new cross-layer design methods are needed.

entry.title: How to revoke users in encryption schemes
entry.summary: How to Revoke Users in Encryption Schemes? IACR ePrint · Nov 8, 2026This paper proposes a way to revoke users from encryption schemes that keeps keys and access rules unchanged, is anonymous and collusion-resistant, and adds only succinct ciphertext overhead. Revoking a user publishes a single random-looking pseudonym without revealing whose key was revoked, and the revocation authority cannot decrypt. Building on the witness encryption framework of Garg et al. (CRYPTO 2025), the authors design two reusable succinct non-membership gadgets and apply them to add revocation to arbitrary public-key encryption and to several advanced encryption schemes.

entry.title: Quantum-safe network design using certified randomness distribution
entry.summary: Designing Quantum-Safe Network Architectures via Certified Randomness Distribution IACR ePrint · Nov 8, 2026This paper proposes an alternative design for quantum-safe network architectures based on distributing certified randomness generated by quantum random number generators (QRNGs) of different trust levels. The modular approach combines high-trust entropy from upper network layers with local contributions to strengthen the security of locally available random sequences. It uses the physical guarantees of QRNGs and symmetric-key algorithms for node authentication, so it can be deployed immediately. The authors argue it avoids the practical security limits of QKD-based solutions and the large key sizes and latency of asymmetric post-quantum cryptography.

entry.title: A lattice-based scheme for threshold batched attribute encryption.
entry.summary: Threshold Batched Attribute-Based Encryption from Succinct LWE IACR ePrint · Nov 8, 2026This paper presents what the authors believe is the first lattice-based candidate for threshold batched attribute-based encryption (TB-ABE), a scheme where decryption is shared among multiple parties. The construction combines a succinct polynomial-digest mechanism from lattice-based batched identity-based encryption, key-homomorphic evaluation for arithmetic-circuit policies, and linear secret sharing. Security is proven under the ℓ-succinct LWE assumption, assuming the underlying ramp threshold sharing scheme has the required share-uniformity property.

entry.title: Paper: Hermite Constants in Dimensions 10, 11 and 12
entry.summary: The Hermite Constants in Dimensions 10, 11 and 12 IACR ePrint · Nov 9, 2026This paper introduces a series of seven papers establishing exact values of the Hermite constants in dimensions 10 and 11 and in dimension 12. The argument relies on the classification of perfect forms of rank nine and explicitly stated computational inputs, treating each dimension in turn. The dimension-12 upper bound follows from Mordell's inequality and is matched by the Coxeter–Todd lattice.

entry.title: A paper on the 11-dimensional Hermite constant: assembling the proof and its certificates
entry.summary: A Focus on Hermite Constant 11 IACR ePrint · Nov 9, 2026This paper assembles the dimension-eleven part of a series on Hermite constants in dimensions ten, eleven and twelve. It reduces a hypothetical lattice to a chain of sections of ranks eleven, ten and nine, and a global finite computation with certificates excludes all but ten candidate forms. It describes four certificate formats and their checking rules, and proves that every valid certificate excludes its form. The resulting bound is γ₁₁ = 4/¹¹√972, conditional on the stated classification, census and finite checks.

entry.title: VeilTune: Secure Fine-Tuning of Private LoRA Adapters on Public Language Models
entry.summary: VeilTune: Secure Fine-Tuning of Private LoRA Adapters on Public Pretrained Language Models arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper shows that existing secure fine-tuning protocols leak intermediate results that let a data owner copy the provider's LoRA adapter from a single training step. It presents VeilTune, described as the first protocol to run backpropagation-based fine-tuning of a pretrained language model entirely inside secure multi-party computation. On four few-shot tasks it is reported to outperform SecP-Tuning in accuracy, and on SST-2 it shows end-to-end speedup and lower communication cost.

entry.title: Shortcuts and Boundaries: Verifiable RL Misalignment and Contextual Safety Learning
entry.summary: Shortcuts and Boundaries: Verifiable RL Misalignment and Contextual Safety Learning arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies reward-driven misalignment in reinforcement learning, where agents learn executable shortcuts that earn more reward than compliant strategies. The authors build diverse interactive environments at scale that encode these reward-context conflicts and derive compliance feedback from execution histories. They report that even a minority of conflict exposure can lead to widespread shortcut acquisition, and that a simple binary penalty from contextual checks partly mitigates violations. The learned safety also transfers to unseen tasks with changing evidence requirements, raising safe completion rates.

entry.title: TUTTI: Fast Parallel CKKS Bootstrapping on CPUs
entry.summary: TUTTI: Parallel CKKS Bootstrapping in under 3 ms on CPU arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper introduces TUTTI, a new CKKS bootstrapping method with lower multi-threaded latency than previous low-latency solutions. It builds on SPRU with improved parallelism and message handling, and includes a refined security analysis of LMSS block-binary secret keys. Reported results show TUTTI bootstrapping 4096 real-number messages in 46 to 83.4 ms on 192 threads, and a single message in 4.6 ms on 32 threads, faster than TFHE-rs at 7.3 ms.

entry.title: Suppression Is Not Erasure: Analysis of LoRA Backdoor Defense Reactivation Limits
entry.summary: Suppression Is Not Erasure: Mechanistic Analysis and Reactivation Boundaries of Subspace Projection for LoRA Backdoor Defense arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper examines defenses that project LoRA adapter weights onto estimated backdoor subspaces to remove hidden triggers. A rank-1 trigger-difference projection drives static attack success to 0%, but the authors show that five-sample few-shot fine-tuning reactivates the backdoor in nearly all evaluated weight-editing defenses. They conclude that low static attack success does not mean the backdoor parameters have been erased.

entry.title: DeepChronos: Time-Aware Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning for Detecting Multi-Step Cyberattacks
entry.summary: DeepChronos: Temporal Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning for Multi-Step Attack Detection arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper presents DeepChronos, a neuro-symbolic network intrusion detection system that combines learned flow-level evidence with explicit attack-phase rules, temporal prerequisites, and previously inferred phases. Instead of detecting events first and correlating them later, it lets the evolving attack history guide each detection decision. Evaluated on DARPA 2000 and AIT-LDS V2, it improves macro F1 over purely neural baselines by up to 11.3%, eliminates causal violations under strict temporal constraints, and keeps inference latency at the millisecond scale.

entry.title: A paper on checking distributed energy resource commands against grid operating context to catch credentialed attacks that static checks miss
entry.summary: Checking DER Commands Against Grid Context Catches Credentialed Attacks Static Checks Miss arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper observes that authorization of distributed energy resource (DER) commands relies on the sender's identity and whether a value has been seen before, so an attacker with valid credentials writing ordinary values can pass. The authors propose judging each DER write against grid operating context, including nearby bus voltages, hour, day-ahead price, system load, and irradiance, compared with operator writes under similar conditions in the feeder's benign history. They evaluate the approach on the IEEE 123-bus and 8500-node feeders against nine attack scenarios.

entry.title: Maurer-Inspired Two-Way Physical-Layer Authentication Against Multi-Antenna Impersonation
entry.summary: Maurer-Inspired Two-Way Physical-Layer Authentication Against Multi-Antenna Impersonation Attacks arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper proposes a two-way physical-layer authentication scheme inspired by Maurer's approach, where Alice must authenticate herself to Bob in the presence of a multi-antenna impersonator, Trudy. Bob and Alice add artificial noise to their transmissions so that Trudy cannot predict Bob's fresh randomness. For quasi-static Gaussian MIMO channels with TDD reciprocity, the authors derive missed-detection bounds for attacks that replace the challenge, the response, or both. With equal antenna numbers at all nodes, they show cases where the scheme achieves lower worst-case missed detection than specified one-way tests.

entry.title: How Far Second-Order Linear Response Predicts Quantization Error: Pre-Registered Tests on Five Language Models
entry.summary: How Far Does Second-Order Linear Response Predict Quantization Mismatch? Pre-Registered Measurements on Five Language Models arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper tests whether a fast screen based on the unquantized model's Fisher information and a second-order expansion can predict the KL divergence caused by weight quantization. Across Qwen3, OLMo-2 and other models using int8, fp8 and int4 formats, relative predictions hold consistently while absolute predictions are less reliable. The authors also trace prediction errors from bf16 gradient computation to arithmetic in the backward pass, which fp32 removes, and build a screener that predicts well on the unseen Mistral-7B-v0.3 family.

entry.title: Bounded delegation for runtime protection reconfiguration in RISC-V microcontrollers
entry.summary: Reconfiguring System-Level Protection Through Bounded Delegation in RISC-V MCUs arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper addresses runtime changes to protection policies in microcontroller-based embedded systems, where existing mechanisms do not limit what policy an authorized domain may create. It proposes an ownership-aware model that uses explicit ownership and rule containment to bound configuration authority and recursive delegation. An open-source RISC-V World Checker integrated into a CVA6-based SoC shows no drop in access latency or operating frequency, with 7.1% LUT and 1.2% FF overhead for eight rules. In an over-the-air update case study, direct reconfiguration reduces policy-transition latency by 89.5% compared with hypervisor mediation and 94.6% compared with trusted firmware mediation.

entry.title: Double-Blind Evals: A Method for Mutually Confidential AI Safety Audits
entry.summary: Double Blind Evals: Resolving the Dual Confidentiality Dilemma in AI Safety Auditing arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper proposes "double-blind evals," a method that keeps an evaluator's test prompts hidden from the model owner while also protecting the owner's model weights and inference code. It uses secure enclaves that encrypt data in RAM at the hardware level. In a pilot, the authors evaluated Google DeepMind's proprietary Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite against part of the private AILuminate benchmark, running on an NVIDIA H100 secure enclave on Google Cloud Platform with OpenMined's PySyft.

entry.title: Stealthy system identification under timing limits: a simple static model and how detectable it is
entry.summary: Covert System Identification Under Timing Constraints: A Static Linear Model and Its Detectability Implications arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies how an attacker can learn the dynamics of a cyber-physical system while trying to avoid detection. It proposes a lightweight static linear model in which the time to complete a setpoint change is proportional to the commanded speed difference, and tests it on a Siemens PROFINET testbed. The model captures the drive's ramp response well but misses the terminal overshoot, and that transient is where the attacker's residual is detected by two anomaly monitors. The authors argue that the stealth limit for this model class is tied to the plant's own settling transients under the detector calibration used.

entry.title: Text2NGAC: multi-LLM pipeline extracting NGAC access policies with mutation-tested verification
entry.summary: Text2NGAC: a multi-LLM pipeline for NGAC policy extraction with mutation-based verification arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper presents Text2NGAC, a pipeline of cooperating large language models that converts natural-language access-control policies into NIST Next Generation Access Control (NGAC) graphs. It disambiguates each sentence, escalates uncertain ones to a multi-model ensemble, and checks the extracted graph with a five-strategy verifier whose effectiveness is measured by controlled mutation testing. The authors claim it is the first system to extract all four NGAC relationship types from real-world policy documents. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report the first extraction of all four NGAC relationship types from real policy documents, with mutation-tested verification and 97.3-99.6% accuracy across corpora.

entry.title: Hidden in Plain Sight: Register-Renaming-Based Privacy-Enhanced Computing
entry.summary: Hidden in Plain Sight: Privacy-Enhanced Computing Through Register Renaming arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper introduces HPS-PEC, a method that achieves privacy-enhanced computing by reusing existing CPU register renaming and register file infrastructure with minor architectural changes. Across 25 VIP-Bench benchmarks using a 7-cycle QARMA-64 cipher, encrypted code runs at 3.41x the execution time of unprotected native code (geometric mean). It is 1.26x faster than a Sequestered Encryption unit while using under a third of its dedicated area.

entry.title: ML Models Are Not Ciphers: Why Power Analysis Struggles to Extract Model Weights
entry.summary: ML Models Are Not Ciphers: Power Analysis for Weight Extraction Is Harder Than You Think arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper asks whether power-analysis attacks from cryptography can reveal the secret weights of machine-learning models. It challenges the approach of treating models as ciphers and examines recovering all layers of fully trained networks, assuming an idealized adversary who observes leakage without noise. The authors find that limited-precision floating-point arithmetic, low-diffusion linear operations, and the reduction of data entropy in models make weight recovery, especially in deep layers, require unexpectedly many traces.

entry.title: A short guide to post-quantum cryptography for industrial use
entry.summary: Brief introduction to post-quantum cryptography in industrial applications arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper reviews how post-quantum cryptography (PQC) is being adopted in industries including IoT, healthcare, civil infrastructure, and defense. It gives a self-contained introduction to PQC and its market position, and reports implementation experiments on selected quantum-safe methods, including the quantum resources needed to break common schemes. The authors also discuss the quantum-attack resistance of different PQC classes and the status of PQC implementations across programming languages. Benchmark results for KEM and signature algorithms are provided to help choose an algorithm based on performance, data lifetime, and sensitivity.

entry.title: "Say Shibboleth": Using decoy traps to identify the LLMs and harnesses behind AI cyberattacks
entry.summary: Say Shibboleth: Fingerprinting the LLMs and Harnesses Behind Agentic Attacks arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper studies how to infer, from telemetry, which LLM version and execution harness an agentic cyberattacker is using. The authors introduce shibboleth traps, modular honeypot services that elicit discriminative behaviors, and probes that reveal harness-specific execution traits through effects visible in later requests. Combining declarative and behavioral signals identifies among 15 candidate models with about 90% average top-1 accuracy, and fixed probe rules identify the correct harness in four tested harnesses with 92% accuracy. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose shibboleth honeypot traps and harness probes, reporting about 90% top-1 accuracy over 15 models and 92% over four harnesses.

entry.title: Detecting Shadow AI: Finding Unapproved AI Agents on Company Computers
entry.summary: Detecting Shadow AI: Unsanctioned LLM Agents on Enterprise Endpoints: A Taxonomy, an Open Detector and a Controlled Evaluation arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper examines unapproved autonomous AI agents used inside organisations, a problem it calls shadow AI. It proposes a taxonomy of nine agent classes and six layers of endpoint traces, and presents Agent Detector, an open-source Windows tool that combines service identity with configuration, installation and execution history. In a controlled test, behaviour-only rules flagged every benign look-alike program, while Agent Detector flagged none and detected agents in most runs.

entry.title: A flexible encryption scheme combining homomorphic encryption and ML-KEM to protect health data during processing
entry.summary: An Agile Homomorphic Encryption and ML-KEM Scheme for Privacy-Preserving Health Data Processing arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper addresses privacy concerns in storing and processing health data by proposing an agile cryptographic scheme that combines ML-KEM, a post-quantum key-encapsulation standard, with BGV, a fully homomorphic encryption scheme. The scheme is designed for efficient implementation in embedded use cases. The authors describe their parameter selection and demonstrate feasibility with a proof-of-concept implementation.

entry.title: A Explicit Bound for Shamir's Secret Sharing Under Local Leakage
entry.summary: An Explicit Below Half Threshold Bound for the Local Leakage Resilience of Shamir's Secret Sharing Scheme arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper studies how many shares Shamir's secret sharing scheme over prime fields needs to resist arbitrary 1-bit local leakage from each party. The authors show that for sufficiently large n and any prime p greater than n, the (n,t) scheme is exp(-Ω(n))-resilient whenever t/n is at least 0.489, for any distinct nonzero evaluation points. The proof refines dual-code list recovery analysis and combines complementary Fourier estimates based on the support sizes and biases of the leakage functions.

entry.title: Public, identifiable, and practically permanent: ethics lessons from arXiv research
entry.summary: Public, Identifiable, and Effectively Immutable: Ethical Lessons from Research on arXiv arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper examines the ethical issues raised by research that analyzes arXiv source files, which arXiv distributes publicly, often to the surprise of authors. The authors identify four higher-level dilemmas researchers may face with such data. They distill four lessons: public availability is only the starting point of ethical reasoning, research should limit amplification of exposed information, disclosure should match the harm and actionability of findings, and effective immutability must be considered.

entry.title: Lessons Not Learned: Why Cross-Chain Bridges Keep Losing Billions the Same Way
entry.summary: Lessons Not Learned: Why Cross-Chain Bridges Keep Losing Billions the Same Way arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper catalogues cross-chain bridge hacks from 2021 to 2026 and finds that security posture failures, involving people, code, controls, and off-chain infrastructure, account for 88% of reported losses since 2023, with nearly all repeating earlier failures. The authors propose a bridge security assessment rubric that scores each deployment from on-chain evidence and caps the score at the lowest value when a fatal risk exists. They also build analyzers that apply the rubric to deployed bridges and monitor them for changes.

entry.title: SNAPRAG: A low-cost attack that extracts RAG knowledge bases using adversarial perturbations
entry.summary: SNAPRAG: Cost-Efficient Knowledge Extraction Attack on RAG Systems via Adversarial Perturbations arXiv · Nov 9, 2026Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems pull information from external knowledge bases to improve LLM responses, but repeated querying can let attackers extract much of that private data. This paper proposes SNAPRAG, a cost-efficient extraction attack that generates adversarial queries algorithmically without external LLMs and under a configurable query budget. It uses a discrete token-mutation algorithm in a strict black-box setting and adaptive dissimilarity threshold calibration to reach unexplored semantic regions. The authors report needing up to 6.77 times fewer queries to extract half the knowledge base, recovering up to 96.9% within a fixed budget, and remaining the leading attack against four of five active defenses.

entry.title: GPU-accelerated encrypted neural network training using batched diagonal packing
entry.summary: GPU-Accelerated Non-Interactive Encrypted Neural Network Training with Batched Diagonal Packing arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper presents a Rust implementation of CKKS homomorphic encryption for training neural networks, with training and bootstrapping ciphertext arithmetic running on the GPU. On the main MNIST model over 100 updates, training time falls from 14,268.295 to 293.075 seconds, a 48.68 times speedup over the authors' CPU implementation, with identical decoded parameters and predictions. A separate GPU run of ten passes over 4,800 images reaches 90.35% test accuracy against 90.41% for the plaintext twin. Parameter agreement is verified only at 100 updates, and comparisons with the ReBoot baseline are conditional.

entry.title: StealthyPoison: Covertly Corrupting Third-Party Skills to Steer LLM Agent Behavior
entry.summary: StealthyPoison: Manipulating LLM Agent Behavior through Procedural Poisoning of Third-Party Skills arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper presents StealthyPoison, an attack that poisons the procedures of third-party skills used by LLM agents, altering decision-critical rules so tasks produce incorrect outcomes while the skill still appears to work normally. The attack builds reusable poisoned procedures without access to real user requests, using synthesized requests and a surrogate agent for feedback, and augments retrieval metadata to improve selection. Evaluated on 566 target skills and 5,244 requests, it raises top-1 poisoned-skill placement by 13.6% over HotFlip and GCG. The authors report that the payloads transfer to three held-out victim models and that most evade detection by SkillSpector and GPT-5.4-mini. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce reusable stealthy procedural poisoning of third-party skills without target user requests, plus metadata augmentation for retrieval; they report gains over HotFlip and GCG across

entry.title: FALC: A model of AI forensic evidence across the AI life cycle and a research agenda
entry.summary: FALC: An Artifact-Centric Life Cycle Model and Research Agenda for AI Forensics arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper introduces the Forensic AI Life Cycle (FALC), a model that focuses on the forensic artifacts produced during an AI system's life cycle rather than on the life cycle stages themselves. From it, the authors derive a reference list of artifacts useful to investigations and collect crime examples involving AI along with likely investigative questions. They also propose a taxonomy of forensic fields based on whether established techniques can currently analyze these artifacts.

entry.title: A UAV-assisted system that performs encrypted computation on wireless data to protect privacy.
entry.summary: A Privacy-Preserving UAV-Assisted Secure Wireless Communication and Computing System Based on Fully Homomorphic Encryption arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper proposes a UAV-assisted secure computing framework that combines CKKS fully homomorphic encryption with multi-party secure computation to protect the computation process over wireless channels. The UAV separates key distribution from encrypted computation, supporting encrypted weighted aggregation, encrypted matrix multiplication, and encrypted decision tree inference. Experiments report better time and space efficiency than BFV, BGV, and SHE schemes for certain operations, along with high numerical precision for weighted aggregation.

entry.title: Harness Matters: Measuring How Execution Frameworks Shape Web Agent Security
entry.summary: Harness Matters: Measuring and Dissecting Security Resilience in Web Agents arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper studies how the execution harness of web agents affects their security. The authors divide harnesses into four stages (goal interpretation, webpage perception, reasoning and planning, and action execution) and build WebTrap Farm, an evaluation framework covering malicious user prompts, malicious prompt injection, and deceptive web design. The results show that existing harnesses remain vulnerable to typical attacks, and that both the harness and the backend model significantly influence security outcomes.

entry.title: Spectral Unlearning: Structure-Preserving Weight Updates for Language Models
entry.summary: Spectral Unlearning: Transformer Structure-Preserving Updates for Language Models arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper addresses machine unlearning in large language models, which aims to remove specific knowledge or behaviors while keeping the model useful. The authors propose spectral unlearning, which combines standard unlearning objectives with matrix-structured optimization that respects the matrix form of transformer weights. They show that the spectral update matches the steepest-descent direction for transformers built from linear layers with normalized inputs and outputs. Evaluated on memorization, privacy, and utility via their harmonic mean, the method consistently outperforms baselines and closes most of the gap to a retain-trained reference.

entry.title: Research on scaling adaptive prompt injection attacks using agent swarms
entry.summary: Scaling Adaptive Prompt Injection Attacks with Agent Swarms arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper studies prompt injection attacks against AI agents. The authors build a synthetic evaluation dataset that uses random non-malicious actions as adversarial goals, to measure whether models respect instruction hierarchy. They show that a more capable agentic attacker can reliably get models to follow instructions embedded in tool output, including models previously considered robust on public benchmarks. The authors argue that frontier defenses may need proactive, automated red-teaming.

entry.title: Efficient private information retrieval protocols built on modular forms
entry.summary: Doubly-Efficient Private Information Retrieval from Modular Forms arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper presents multi-server private information retrieval protocols in which each server answers queries in sublinear time and stores only one extra bit beyond a preprocessing structure of n+1 bits. For two servers, server time drops to n^0.82 while storage shrinks from O(n√log n) to n+1 bits. With three or more servers, the protocols also reduce server time compared with prior information-theoretic schemes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors generalize matching-vector techniques to degree-two exponent computations and build Fourier-sparse functions via modular forms, reporting improved server time and n+1-bit storage.

entry.title: Ultrasound-based biometric watermarking to defend facial videos against deepfakes
entry.summary: Ultrasound-Assisted Biometric Watermarking Against Face Video Deepfakes arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper proposes UltraGuard, a biometric video watermarking method that protects facial videos from deepfakes in real time. It uses a smartphone's built-in speaker and microphone to emit ultrasonic signals and capture biometric features, which are fused with spatio-temporal dynamic features of the video and embedded as a watermark. The authors report that the approach can defend against forgery and editing attacks both at the source and during propagation, and suggest it could be deployed on users' mobile devices.

entry.title: Advantage Distillation for Paired-State Quantum Key Distribution
entry.summary: Advantage Distillation in Paired-State Quantum Key Distribution arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper studies advantage distillation for paired-state Loop-Back quantum key distribution, linking a fixed optical station with a portable terminal. It uses two independent public parity checks on a minimal connected graph to select consistent blocks of three two-bit records, and derives acceptance probabilities, residual-error laws and retention rates. A modular security theorem bounds the extra guessing advantage an adversary can gain after syndrome disclosure and block acceptance.

entry.title: ShadowBench-MCP: Measuring hidden risky tool calls in LLM routing
entry.summary: ShadowBench-MCP: Measuring Shadow Invocations in MCP-Style Tool Routing arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper studies how LLM agents acting as tool routers can be steered, through task-preserving request variants, onto riskier execution paths that skip safety tools such as validation, provenance, or audit. The authors introduce ShadowBench-MCP, a benchmark and metric suite that combines task-preservation, operational-pressure, and route-drift measures into a pre-execution score. In a single-router policy ablation, efficiency-first routing showed a 29.2% shadow-invocation rate, while policy-aware routing reduced it to 4.2%. The authors present these as early evidence from one router rather than a claim of universal vulnerability.

entry.title: Public-key encryption built on the planted clique conjecture and noisy k-LIN over expanders
entry.summary: Using the Planted Clique Conjecture for Cryptography: Public-Key Encryption from Planted Clique and Noisy k-mathsfLIN Over Expanders arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper presents a public-key encryption scheme that is provably secure against polynomial-size adversaries. It relies on the standard planted clique conjecture at hardness level n^{log^α n} for any α in (0,1), together with a milder conjecture about noisy k-LIN over expanders. Both conjectures are average-case versions of NP-complete problems studied for decades. The scheme answers an open question posed by Applebaum, Barak, and Wigderson at STOC 2010.

entry.title: Injecting attacks into vehicle messages to study how traffic reacts
entry.summary: Attack Injection to Vehicle Reactions: Extensible Closed-Loop Adversarial Evaluation Framework arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper presents an extensible closed-loop adversarial evaluation framework built on the VaN3Twin traffic and wireless network simulator. It adds 76 configurable attack profiles, adapted to European Telecommunications Standards Institute (ETSI) message formats and organized into nine suites, along with a labelled dataset. Evaluation shows that attacked messages drive vehicle reactions, which can then influence other vehicles through subsequent unmodified messages.

entry.title: Delegating computation with approximate arithmetic: interactive proofs where both sides use floating-point numbers
entry.summary: Delegating Computation with Approximate Arithmetic: Interactive Proofs for Wizards arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper studies interactive proofs for arithmetic circuits over complex numbers, where both prover and verifier compute approximately. The goal is to show that a claimed output is close to the exact result. It extends the GKR protocol to this approximate setting, and the authors claim these are the first doubly efficient interactive proofs in which both parties compute approximately. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend GKR to approximate complex arithmetic by labeling gates with roots of unity, reporting doubly efficient interactive proofs with polynomial overhead.

entry.title: Treating the Model as an Untrusted Component: Enforcing Deterministic Policies, Human Approval and Taint Tracking Against Prompt Injection in Tool-Using AI Agents
entry.summary: Treating the Model as an Untrusted Component: Deterministic Policy Enforcement, Human Approval and Taint Tracking Against Prompt Injection in Tool-Using Agents, with Validation on Open-Weights Models arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper studies how to defend tool-using large language model agents against prompt injection, where instructions hidden in data the agent reads can trigger harmful actions. It compares defenses inside the prompt with deterministic policy enforcement outside the model, human approval, and taint tracking, evaluated in a 13-task, 12-tool environment using an oracle independent of each defense. Experiments with two open-weights Qwen2.5 models show that a task-bound monitor blocks most attacks, though the results have limits. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors treat the model as untrusted, enforcing deterministic monitors, approval, and taint tracking against prompt injection, with real open-weights model runs.

entry.title: PRISM: Trimming AI Agent Tool Permissions via Causal Counterfactuals and Information Bottleneck Roles
entry.summary: PRISM: Causal Counterfactual Minimization of Agent Tool Privileges via Information Bottleneck Role Induction arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper applies role engineering to large language model agents rather than human users, addressing over-authorization when agents receive full tool privileges through the Model Context Protocol. PRISM tests whether each tool is necessary for a task using sandbox interventions, compresses agent trajectories into discrete roles via an information bottleneck, and sets the role count at the knee of the rate-distortion curve. Pruning is cast as a bilevel Stackelberg game solved with a generative flow network. On AgentDojo, τ-bench and ToolEmu, PRISM reduces authorized tools per role by 78.3%, reports a 78.2% task success rate, 88.7% counterfactual necessity accuracy, and a 15.9% blast radius.

entry.title: Relative Security of Prompt Injection: Formal Definitions and Defences for LLM Agents
entry.summary: On the Relative Security of Prompt Injection: Mechanised Definitions, Defences and Verdicts for LLM Agents arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper addresses LLM agents that read untrusted content, such as emails or web pages, and may follow hidden instructions within it. It defines security relative to a reference agent that runs the same plan under the same monitor but never obeys untrusted content: an agent is relatively secure if all its leaks are already leaks of the reference. The authors present PlanTERS, a framework with a small agent language, composition with runtime monitors, and attacker models that differ in what they observe. A fence theorem is proved, and relative security of agents with fences, budgets, approvals, loops and dual LLMs is proved or refuted in Isabelle/HOL. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose PlanTERS, a relative-security framework for LLM agent prompt injection, with a fence theorem mechanised in Isabelle/HOL.

entry.title: EVAX: A Practical, Proactive, Adaptive Processor Architecture for Performance and Security
entry.summary: EVAX: Towards a Practical, Pro-active & Adaptive Architecture for High Performance & Security arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper presents an end-to-end approach to defend against known microarchitectural attacks, including speculative execution, fault-injection, covert and side-channel attacks, as well as evasive and zero-day variants. It applies defenses only when attacks are detected, cutting the overhead of existing defenses by over 95%. Using a generative framework called Evasion Vaccination (EVAX), it trains ML detectors and engineers security-centric performance counters. Reported overheads are 1.26% for InvisiSpec and 3.45% for Fencing, with about 4 false positives per million instructions. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report on-demand defense activation with a generative framework for training detectors, cutting InvisiSpec and Fencing overheads substantially across several attack classes.

entry.title: Robust, private swarm learning with zero-knowledge validator admission and consensus aggregation
entry.summary: Robust and Private Swarm Learning via Zero-Knowledge Validator Admission and Consensus Aggregation arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper proposes a swarm learning framework where validators must first pass a zero-knowledge attestation showing a reference model ran correctly on their private data, without revealing samples. Admitted validators reach Byzantine fault-tolerant consensus on gradient masks and quality-based aggregation weights. Across four non-IID benchmarks, the method matches FedAvg on clean data and, under a gradient-scaling attack, retains 94% of clean accuracy on CIFAR-100 and over 99% on FashionMNIST, where FedAvg reaches 2.1% and 11%.

entry.title: Study on whether AI coding agents copy existing security flaws into new code
entry.summary: Coding Agents Propagate Vulnerabilities in Code Bases arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper examines whether LLM-based coding agents introduce vulnerabilities similar to those already present in a code base. The authors test 96 backend implementation tasks and 20 pairs of repository-level C/C++ tasks. They find that insecure existing code leads agents to write vulnerable code more often, with agents using existing flaws as templates.

entry.title: When coding AI agents control robot arms: safety risks across digital and physical worlds
entry.summary: When Coding Agents Get Arms: Safety Risks Across the Digital-Physical Boundary arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper introduces ArmedAgent, the first systematic benchmark for evaluating safety risks when coding agents control a real robot arm zero-shot, without task-specific demonstrations or retraining. It covers robustness, malicious use, and indirect prompt injection across 36 tasks in 5 scenarios, tested in simulation and validated on a physical robot arm. Testing several frontier models under common agent frameworks, the authors find substantial safety risks in current systems. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a benchmark for zero-shot robot-arm coding agents covering misuse and indirect injection, validated in simulation and on a physical arm.

entry.title: RoCoMark: A robust code watermarking method resisting LLM-based functionality-preserving rewriting attacks
entry.summary: RoCoMark: Robust Code Watermarking Against LLM-Based Functionality-Preserving Rewriting Attacks arXiv · Nov 8, 2026This paper addresses the problem that watermarks in generated code are often lost when large language models rewrite it while keeping its function. It proposes RoCoMark, a code watermarking framework in which the embedder and an LLM rewriter play a multi-round minimax game, with an adaptive attack-evolution mechanism based on Reflexion and memory pools. On four benchmarks against attacks generated by five LLMs, it reports an average detection AUROC of 74.2%, a Rewrite BitACC of 75.3%, and a functionality pass rate above 99.7%.

entry.title: Self-healing system design inspired by the immune system for autonomous cyber resilience
entry.summary: Self-Healing by design: Immune-system inspired autonomous cyber resilience arXiv · Nov 8, 2026This paper explores how autonomous cyber resilience methods inspired by the human immune system can be combined with resilience mechanisms in naval and aeronautical maneuvering systems. Using TNO's OpPic application, it shows how TNO's Self-Healing for Cyber Security software can provide mission- and threat-adaptive resilience. Based on this, the authors derive six guidelines for designing autonomous cyber-resilient systems.

entry.title: Breaking Slide Puzzle CAPTCHAs with GAN-Generated Trajectories
entry.summary: Attacking Slide Puzzle CAPTCHAs Based on Time and Space Generative Adversarial Networks arXiv · Nov 8, 2026This paper systematically analyzes the defense strategies of six popular slide puzzle CAPTCHAs: Capy, Dingxiang, Geetest, Kyger, Shumei and Tencent.
